dashboardCard.title: Platform usage guide
dashboardCard.subtitle: Learn how to create courses, classes, activities and more.

createCourse.title: How to create a course
createCourse.description: Courses are the main structure of the platform. Each course contains modules and classes.

steps.0: In the side menu, access "Manage Courses" (administrative area).
steps.1: Click the "New Course" button in the top right corner of the page.
steps.2: Fill in the title, description and, if desired, set a deadline.
steps.3: Upload a cover image by clicking on the thumbnail area.
steps.5: Click "Save" to create the course. It already appears in the list, but still without content.

createCourse.context: A course is the main structure of your school. It is the product that students purchase or access. Everything you will teach — modules, classes, activities — is organized within a course.
createCourse.mentalFlow: Before creating the course, think: what is the central theme? Who is the ideal student? What result will he have when finished? Your course name and description should communicate exactly that.
createCourse.expectedResult: The course appears in the Manage Courses listing and in the school's public showcase. Students can now view it, but there are no classes available yet.

commonMistakes.0: Creating the course without defining a clear description — this confuses the student when choosing.
commonMistakes.1: Use a generic title like “Course 1” rather than something descriptive like “Fundamentals of Technical Analysis.”
commonMistakes.2: Leave the deadline very tight before configuring all the content.

tips.0: Tip: Write the description with the student in mind, not the content. Ex: "At the end of this course, you will be able to..."
tips.1: Tip: Create the course first, even without content. This way you can already configure everything before releasing it to students.

createLessons.title: How to create modules and classes
createLessons.description: Within each course, you organize the content into modules. Each module groups together related classes.

steps.0: In the course listing, click "Manage" on the desired course.
steps.1: You will see the classes screen, divided into modules.
steps.2: To create a module, click on "New module" and enter the title.
steps.3: Within a module, click "New Class" to add a class.
steps.4: Fill in the class title and, optionally, video and supporting material.
steps.5: Use the "Access Rules" panel to set prerequisites and release date.
steps.6: When expanding a class, you will see the list of steps (content and activities).

createLessons.context: Modules are thematic groups within the course — they function like chapters. Each module contains classes. Each class is a learning unit with content and activities.
createLessons.mentalFlow: Think about the student’s journey: what do they need to learn first? Arrange the modules in order of increasing complexity. Within each module, organize classes in the same way: theory before practice.
createLessons.expectedResult: The course now has visible modules, with classes within each module. Once steps are added, students can consume the content in sequence.

commonMistakes.0: Creating all classes in a single module — loses thematic organization.
commonMistakes.1: Name classes as "Class 1", "Class 2" without indicating the subject.
commonMistakes.2: Do not use prerequisites when the class depends on previous knowledge.

tips.0: Tip: Start with a short introductory module (1–2 lessons) to quickly engage the learner before jumping into dense content.
tips.1: Tip: use the release date to create a delivery schedule, releasing modules week by week.

reorder.title: How to reorder classes and steps
reorder.description: The order of modules, classes and steps can be rearranged by drag and drop.

steps.0: On a course's classes screen, find the six-dot icon (⠿) next to each item.
steps.1: Click and hold the icon to activate drag mode.
steps.2: Drag up or down to the desired position and release.
steps.3: The order is automatically saved after dropping the item.
steps.4: The same mechanism works within each class to reorder the content steps.

reorder.context: The order of classes and steps defines the student's learning sequence. The system strictly follows this order — the student goes through the steps one by one within each class.
reorder.mentalFlow: Think of each step as a mini-step. The ideal sequence is: context → theory (text/video) → practice (activity). You can rearrange at any time, but the change immediately impacts the student experience.
reorder.expectedResult: The new sequence is saved immediately. The student will see the content in the updated order the next time they access it.

commonMistakes.0: Putting activities before theory — the student has no basis for responding.
commonMistakes.1: Leave the introductory content in the middle of the module.
commonMistakes.2: Reordering classes that students have already started without warning — can cause confusion in progress.

tips.0: Tip: the ideal sequence within a class is usually: text content → video → fixation activity.
tips.1: Tip: Use students' progress history to identify where they get stuck and reorganize the content.

createActivities.title: How to create activities
createActivities.description: Activities are interactive exercises added as steps within a lesson. They can be of multiple types.

steps.0: Open a class from the class management screen.
steps.1: Click the "Add Step" button at the end of the step list.
steps.3: Choose the type of activity: Multiple choice, True/False, Ordering, Trading simulation, among others.
steps.4: Set the title and review policy (immediate, after date, or never).
steps.5: Once created, click on "Questions" to add the questions and answers for the activity.
steps.6: Click save. The activity appears in the steps list.
steps.7: Click on "Questions" next to the activity to add questions and alternatives.

createActivities.context: Activities are interactive exercises that the student responds to during class. They exist to secure learning, validate knowledge and generate progress. Without activities, the student has no grade or progress recorded.
createActivities.mentalFlow: Choose the type of activity according to what you want to evaluate: multiple choice for concepts, true/false for myths, ordering for processes, trading simulation for market practice. Each type has a specific purpose.
createActivities.expectedResult: The activity appears in the sequence of steps in the class. The student will need to answer it to advance. The result and grade are recorded in the progress.

commonMistakes.0: Create the activity but do not add questions — it is empty and the student cannot answer.
commonMistakes.1: Always use the same type of activity — vary it to maintain engagement.
commonMistakes.2: Not correctly defining the review policy — students don’t know if they got it right or wrong.

tips.0: Tip: Use "Multiple Choice" for quick concepts and "Trading Simulation" for practice lessons — the combination greatly increases retention.
tips.1: Tip: Add a short activity (3–5 questions) at the end of each lesson, not just at the end of the module.

createContent.title: How to create presentations and content
createContent.description: In addition to activities, you can add content steps: text, video or image.

steps.0: Open a class from the management screen.
steps.1: Click "Add step" and select the "Content" tab.
steps.2: Choose the type: Text, Video or Image.
steps.3: A modal will open for you to enter the title and corresponding content.
steps.4: After saving, the step appears in the list and can be freely reordered.
steps.5: Content steps are displayed to the student in the defined sequence, interspersed with the activities.
steps.6: Define the step title (e.g. "Introduction to technical analysis") and click save.
steps.7: The step appears in the list and can be dragged to the correct position.

createContent.context: Content steps are the blocks of theory within a lesson: explanatory text, video or image. They appear before activities and are the main learning vehicle before practice.
createContent.mentalFlow: A content step must have a single focus. Don't try to put everything into one giant text — create separate steps for each block of information. The student takes one step at a time.
createContent.expectedResult: The content appears following the class. The student sees each step in order, with a forward button between them. Completed steps are marked in the progress.

commonMistakes.0: Create a single pass of very long text — break it into smaller parts to make it easier to read.
commonMistakes.1: Don't add alt text to images — affects accessibility.
commonMistakes.2: Mix content from different topics in the same text step.

tips.0: Tip: use short videos (up to 10 minutes) to explain the concept and text to summarize the main points below.
tips.1: Tip: The text field accepts plain HTML — use <b> for highlights and <ul>/<li> for topic lists.

lab.title: How to use the laboratory
lab.description: The laboratory allows you to practice operations in a simulation environment, without risk. You configure the simulation parameters and operate on the terminal.

steps.0: In the side menu, click on "Laboratory".
steps.1: Configure the simulation parameters: number of candles, timeframe, volatility, trend, spread and initial balance.
steps.2: Click "Start simulation" to open the trading terminal.
steps.3: In the terminal, you can view the candle chart and execute buy and sell orders.
steps.4: When you end the session, the result is saved in the history.
steps.5: Access the simulation history via the "History" link on the laboratory screen.
steps.6: Access history via the "History" link on the lab screen to review previous sessions.

lab.context: The laboratory is a trading simulation environment without real money. It exists so that the student can practice executing orders — buying and selling — under realistic market conditions, without financial risk. It's the equivalent of a flight simulator before actually flying.
lab.mentalFlow: Before starting, configure the scenario according to what you want to train: more volatile markets to practice emotional management, defined trends to practice entries in favor of the trend, or sideways markets to practice range trading.
lab.expectedResult: When you finish a session, you will see the result: accumulated PnL, maximum drawdown, number of trades and success rate. This data is saved in the history to monitor progress.

commonMistakes.0: Always use the same parameters — vary to train in different market conditions.
commonMistakes.1: Ignore the drawdown — risk control is part of the training, not just the profit.
commonMistakes.2: Close the terminal before ending the session correctly — the result may not be saved.

tips.0: Tip: start with few candles (50–100) and low spread to familiarize yourself with the interface before simulating more complex scenarios.
tips.1: Tip: Use +0.5 or -0.5 trend to simulate markets with clear direction — ideal for beginners to practice trend entries.

buy.description: Purchase order. You profit when the price rises after the purchase. Open a LONG position.

sell.description: Sales order. Allows you to "sell short" (short) — you profit when the price drops. Open a SHORT position.

market.description: Executes immediately at the current market price. Faster, but may have slippage.

limit.description: Executes only if the price reaches the defined value. BUY LIMIT: executes below the defined price. SELL LIMIT: above.

stop.description: Executes when the price reaches the trigger. BUY STOP: purchase above the current level (breakout). SELL STOP: sell below.

sl.description: Price level that closes your position automatically to limit losses. Fundamental for risk management.

tp.description: Price level that closes your position automatically to guarantee profit. Helps to realize gains.

pnl.description: Profit or loss from your operation. Positive PnL = profit. Negative = loss. Shown in $ and %.

equity.description: Your balance + PnL of open positions. Reflects the real value of your account in real time.

position.description: When you have an open operation. LONG = long (bet on the rise). SHORT = sold (bet on the fall). FLAT = no position.

fee.description: Cost per operation charged for each execution (fill). Measured in bps (basis points). 1 bps = 0.01%.

slippage.description: Difference between expected price and actual execution price. Automatically simulated by the engine.

spread.description: Difference between the purchase (ask) and sale (bid) price. Implicit cost of operating.

drawdown.description: Decrease in equity in relation to the maximum peak. Measures the worst moment of your operation. Lower = better risk management.

winrate.description: Percentage of winning trades. 60%+ is considered good. However, it also depends on the risk/return relationship.

sharpe.description: Measures risk-adjusted return. >1 = good, >2 = excellent. Penalizes large fluctuations in results.

profitfactor.description: Sum of gains ÷ sum of losses. >1 = profitable. >2 = consistent strategy.

chart.title: Understand the Chart
chart.description: This is the candlestick chart. Each candle represents a period of time. Green candle = price has risen. Red candle = price has fallen. The body shows opening/closing and the wicks show high/low.

playback.title: Playback Controls
playback.description: Use the Play/Pause buttons to advance the sails automatically. The "→" button advances one candle at a time. Adjust the speed (0.5× to 4×). Observe the market before trading!

order.title: Abra sua Primeira Ordem
order.description: In the "New Order" panel, choose BUY or SELL. Select the type: MARKET (immediate), LIMIT (specific price) or STOP (trigger). Set the quantity and optionally Stop-Loss (SL) and Take-Profit (TP).

position.title: Acompanhe sua Posição
position.description: After an order is filled, its position appears on the side panel. Track PnL in real time. Use the "Close" button to close the position at any time.

tabs.title: Orders, Fills and Metrics
tabs.description: At the bottom: "Orders" shows pending orders (LIMIT/STOP). "Fills" shows all runs performed. "Metrics" shows statistics of your performance (Win Rate, Sharpe, etc.).

submit.title: Finalize and Send
submit.description: When all candles are displayed, the "Submit Result" button appears. Click to submit your simulation to the server. It recalculates everything and generates your final score. Good luck!
